# Procurement Approval Policy P01

Effective January 15, 2026. Owner: Acme Corporation, Procurement Office, California.

## 1. Purpose

This policy governs how the Order Management System and the Invoice Ledger
request, approve, and settle supplier purchases. Every purchase above the
micro-purchase floor must cite a business purpose before funds are reserved.
The Procurement Officer reviews each request for completeness within two
business days of submission. Incomplete requests return to the requestor with
written reasons. All approvals are recorded in the Order Management System so
that auditors can reconstruct who approved what and when. This section exists
to keep spending visible and to prevent duplicate orders across departments.

## 2. Approval thresholds

2.1 Purchases up to $5,000 require one approval from the requestor's Manager.
2.2 Purchases from $5,001 to $50,000 require two approvals: the requestor's
Manager and the Procurement Officer. Amounts in this band must include at
least two competing quotes attached to the order record.
2.3 Purchases above $50,000 require three approvals: the requestor's Manager,
the Procurement Officer, and the Finance Administrator. The Finance
Administrator verifies budget availability in the Invoice Ledger before the
final signature. Emergency purchases above $50,000 follow the same chain but
may collect signatures within five business days after the order ships.
2.4 Recurring subscriptions renew automatically unless the Procurement Officer
cancels them thirty days before the renewal date of March 1, 2026.

## 3. Systems of record

3.1 The Order Management System is the system of record for purchase intent.
Every approved request creates an OrderHeader row before any supplier contact.
3.2 The Invoice Ledger is the system of record for settlement. No invoice
settles without a matching OrderHeader reference and a recorded approval
chain. Jane Smith, Procurement Officer, audits unmatched invoices weekly.
3.3 The Party Directory holds supplier identities. New suppliers need a Party
record with tax jurisdiction before their first purchase order. Suppliers
operating in California must also file a state resale certificate.

## 4. Operational procedure

4.1 The requestor drafts the order in the Order Management System and attaches
quotes, statements of work, and delivery dates. Drafts older than fourteen
days expire automatically and must be recreated from scratch.
4.2 The Manager approves or rejects within three business days. Rejections
must state a reason; silent rejections escalate to the Procurement Officer on
the fourth day. Approved drafts lock their line items against editing.
4.3 The Procurement Officer confirms policy compliance, checks the approval
threshold band, and releases the order to the supplier. Releases happen only
on business days between 9am and 5pm Pacific. Same-day rush releases need a
written justification countersigned by the Finance Administrator.
4.4 Receiving confirms delivery against the order lines within two business
days of arrival. Short shipments create a follow-up task assigned to the
supplier contact within the Party Directory. Over-shipments are quarantined
until the Procurement Officer decides to accept or return them.

## 5. Compliance and review

This policy is reviewed every September by the Procurement Officer together
with the Finance Administrator. Violations are reported to Acme Corporation
leadership within five business days of discovery. Repeat violations trigger a
spending freeze for the offending department until retraining completes. Audit
evidence lives in the Order Management System and the Invoice Ledger for a
minimum of seven years. Questions about interpretation go to the Procurement
Office in writing; verbal guidance never overrides this document. Adopted
December 1, 2025, superseding policy P00 in its entirety.

## 6. Exceptions

Exceptions require a written memo signed by the Procurement Officer and the
Finance Administrator before the order ships. Memos cite the policy section
being waived and expire after ninety days. Standing exceptions are reviewed
each quarter and published to all Managers in California.
